subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should non-local device-less WebSocket operator clients authenticated with the shared gateway token/password be allowed to retain operator scopes, and should that be the default or an explicit configured token-scope policy?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally clear these scopes, while the report asks to restore remote shared-token operator.write behavior; choosing between those outcomes changes the Gateway auth trust boundary.

options.title: Use explicit token scopes
options.body: Keep device-less remote scope clearing as the default and land a bounded token-scope configuration for trusted headless deployments.

options.title: Restore remote token retention
options.body: Treat successful shared token/password auth as enough for non-local WebSocket operators to retain requested scopes by default.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep the current behavior and document that remote WebSocket operator clients must pair or use a supported configured scope path.

recommendation.title: Use explicit token scopes
recommendation.body: Keep device-less remote scope clearing as the default and land a bounded token-scope configuration for trusted headless deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open token-scope implementation PR and recently maintained the Gateway connect policy surface.
